input: The selectivity values reported for the benchmark material differ considerably between the two groups, and it is worth examining the conditions behind each value before either one is used. The first group obtains its selectivity from IAST, applying the theory to single-component isotherms that were measured with dry, pure gases. The second group, by contrast, measures mixture breakthrough curves directly and derives selectivity from the amounts retained when the bed is exposed to the mixture of interest. This methodological difference is significant, because single-component isotherms contain no information whatsoever about competition between species for adsorption sites, whereas a breakthrough measurement inherently captures that competition as it unfolds. Moreover, the feed used in the breakthrough experiments contains water vapour, which competes for the same sites and displaces a portion of the adsorbed phase that the dry isotherms would predict. IAST, furthermore, rests on the assumption of an ideal adsorbed phase, an assumption that becomes increasingly questionable when the adsorbed species interact with quite different strengths, as is the case for water and the target component here. Taken together, these considerations help to explain why the dry-basis estimate sits above the mixture measurement: the estimate includes no competing species, while the measurement is shaped by one. On balance, the mixture-based values appear preferable for design work involving feeds that carry moisture, since the measured selectivity already reflects the displacement effect that a dry estimate simply omits. It should be emphasised, however, that this preference is conditional in nature: it rests on the presence of moisture in the feed of interest. Where a feed is dried upstream of the bed, the competing species is removed, and the balance of the argument shifts toward the quality of the isotherm fit and the spreading-pressure integration. What remains unresolved is the magnitude of the displacement at lower moisture contents, a regime in which neither group reports measurements, leaving an important gap that future work will need to address.
target: Selectivity for the benchmark material is reported at two values that differ by more than the stated uncertainty of either, and the difference follows the method. One group estimates selectivity with IAST from single-component isotherms measured on dry gases. The other group measures mixture breakthrough curves and takes selectivity from the retained amounts at the feed composition. A single-component isotherm records the uptake of one gas at a time and carries no information on competition for sites. A breakthrough measurement records the competition directly, because both species are present and the retained amounts settle under the mixture. Water vapour in the second group's feed competes for the same sites and displaces part of the adsorbed phase that the dry isotherms predict. IAST assumes an ideal adsorbed phase, and the assumption is weakest where the adsorbed species differ in interaction strength, as water and the target component do. The direction of the disagreement follows from the feed states: an estimate built on dry, single-gas data stands above a measurement made with a competing species present. Mixture values are preferred for design on feeds that carry moisture, because the measured selectivity already contains the displacement that the dry estimate omits. The preference rests on the feed condition. A feed dried upstream of the bed removes the competing species, and for such a feed the comparison turns instead on the isotherm fit and the spreading-pressure integration behind the IAST estimate. Each reported value is a property of the material under one feed state, stated with that state, and the comparison is between two feed states as much as between two reports. The size of the displacement at low moisture contents remains open, because neither group reports a measurement in that range, and the behaviour between the dry and the humid feed is untested at its lower end.
